section_summary: This section follows Japan’s worsening financial position in spring and summer 1932: weak bank loans, falling gold reserves, budget deficits, and heavy borrowing for operations in Manchuria and Shanghai. Diplomatic telegrams investigate rumors of a Japanese loan in France, while embassy despatches detail supplementary budgets, bond issues, and new financial legislation. The section also contains cross-reference notes, a newspaper clipping, and several incomplete or duplicated document pages.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: U.S. diplomat in Japan; chargé d’affaires ad interim

people.name: Kōzō Tanaka
people.role: Man reported to have confessed to setting fire to the U.S. consulate in Nagasaki

people.name: Stanley K. Hornbeck
people.role: Chief of the State Department’s Far Eastern affairs bureau

people.name: Baron Sakatani
people.role: Member of the Japanese House of Peers

people.name: Mr. Sugiyama
people.role: Proletarian representative in the Japanese Diet

subfiles.title: Commercial Attaché’s cable on local loans and trade
subfiles.about: Municipal loan requests face costly terms while yen depreciation clouds Japan’s trade outlook.
subfiles.summary: Reports loan demand, high interest, bond payments, price increases, and disappointing exports.

subfiles.title: Extracts from Butts’s cable
subfiles.about: The extract surveys Japanese bond, bank, employment, and trade conditions.
subfiles.summary: Notes weak bonds, prospective military borrowing, persistent bank loans, and a rising import surplus.

subfiles.title: Fragment on Japanese foreign obligations and gold reserves
subfiles.about: Foreign loan repayments and bond interest could strain Japan’s limited gold reserves.
subfiles.summary: Estimates obligations above 300 million yen against a gold reserve of 430 million yen.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Lamont letter
subfiles.about: Locates a letter concerning a Japanese finance minister’s cable through Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.summary: Cross-refers to file 793.94/4953.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Tokyo telegram 107
subfiles.about: Locates a telegram predicting a spring bond issue as revenue falls short.
subfiles.summary: Cross-refers to section K of telegram 107.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram 107, section K: Bank loans
subfiles.about: Long-term bank loans remain largely unliquidated, with weak land and industrial collateral.
subfiles.summary: Reports 9.458 billion yen in outstanding bank loans and warns that rapid liquidation could cause bank failures.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to despatch 533
subfiles.about: Locates a despatch on financial measures passed by the Diet.
subfiles.summary: Cross-refers to despatch 533.

subfiles.title: Berlin telegram 77 on rumored Japanese loan in Paris
subfiles.about: An unconfirmed banking rumor claims Japan is negotiating a large loan in Paris.
subfiles.summary: Reports a rumored $200 million loan and explicitly notes the lack of confirmation.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to financial embargo letter
subfiles.about: Locates a letter concerning Consul Dickover’s proposed financial embargo against Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-refers to file 795.94/5019.

subfiles.title: Berlin telegram on Dirksen and the loan rumor
subfiles.about: Dirksen doubts knowledge of a French loan and comments on its possible military meaning.
subfiles.summary: Reports Dirksen’s view that Russo-Japanese tensions had eased and that a large French loan, if floated, could imply war.

subfiles.title: Continuation of Berlin telegram 80
subfiles.about: A source remains optimistic about rumored loan negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Says a source awaits Bülow’s return from Geneva before informing the German government.

subfiles.title: Department telegram to Wilson on a foreign loan
subfiles.about: A Japanese foreign loan might help consolidate Japan’s position in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Connects the reported loan to U.S. and League nonrecognition of the Manchurian situation.

subfiles.title: Paris telegram 243 on the rumored loan
subfiles.about: Paris inquiries find no evidence of Japanese loan negotiations in France.
subfiles.summary: Contacts profess ignorance and consider such a loan difficult to obtain.

subfiles.title: Instruction to repeat Paris telegram 243
subfiles.about: The Department asks Paris to repeat its loan report to Stimson in Geneva.
subfiles.summary: Directs repetition of telegram 243.

subfiles.title: Duplicate copy of Paris telegram 243
subfiles.about: A duplicate records Paris’s inability to substantiate the rumored loan.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the report on secret or nonexistent negotiations.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to despatch 538
subfiles.about: Locates a despatch on the Diet session called to approve emergency financial measures.
subfiles.summary: Cross-refers to proceedings of the Diet.

subfiles.title: Despatch 538 on proceedings of the 61st Diet
subfiles.about: The extraordinary Diet session passed emergency measures for military operations in China.
subfiles.summary: The despatch describes the short March session and limited opposition to military spending. An enclosed address by Foreign Minister Yoshizawa presents Japan’s account of the Shanghai fighting, League deliberations, Manchuria, and relations with China and Western powers. The surviving pages are discontinuous excerpts.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on a proposed French loan and Japanese obligations
subfiles.about: A reported French loan is considered against Japan’s railway debt and wartime deficits.
subfiles.summary: Cites Takahashi’s plan to seek conversion of the South Manchuria Railway sterling loan and estimates substantial new borrowing needs.

subfiles.title: Geneva telegram 141 rejecting loan rumor
subfiles.about: French officials deny that a Japanese loan is contemplated.
subfiles.summary: Tardieu and Aubert dismiss the loan politically and commercially; Aubert confirms with Paris.

subfiles.title: Division summary of revised working budget
subfiles.about: Japan’s revised 1932–33 budget remains out of balance and relies on loans.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes an estimated 69 million yen deficit and likely borrowing beyond the published 90 million yen.

subfiles.title: Despatch 553 budget tables and analysis
subfiles.about: Tables compare Japan’s revised working budget with the preceding Minseitō budget.
subfiles.summary: The excerpt details falling ordinary revenue, changes in departmental spending, and extraordinary revenue from loans. It concludes that further bond issues will probably be required.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to despatch 560
subfiles.about: Locates press reports of a Mitsui and Mitsubishi loan offer to Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: Notes a reported 20 million yen loan offer.

subfiles.title: Department telegram to Stimson aboard Vulcania
subfiles.to: Secretary of State aboard Vulcania, via Gibraltar
subfiles.about: Berlin forwards a Mitsui representative’s claim of progress in Paris loan negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Relays renewed but unverified reports that Mitsui and the Bank of Japan are negotiating in Paris.

subfiles.title: Division summary of supplementary budget
subfiles.about: Japan plans supplementary spending and further estimates for Manchuria and Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Reports an 89 million yen supplement and projected military and foreign affairs requests.

subfiles.title: Despatch 590 on supplementary budget
subfiles.about: The Cabinet approves supplementary estimates ahead of an extraordinary Diet session.
subfiles.summary: The despatch lists departmental appropriations and prospective Manchurian and Shanghai expenses. It also notes funds for policing political crime, industrial measures, and investigations in Manchuria and Mongolia.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to despatch 578
subfiles.about: Locates a broad report on Japan’s financial and economic conditions.
subfiles.summary: Lists banking, debt, trade, reserves, prices, and industries covered.

subfiles.title: Despatch 578: Financial and economic report on Japan
subfiles.about: A detailed report examines Japan’s banking exposure, reserves, prices, industries, and borrowing prospects.
subfiles.summary: The report traces long-standing land, industrial, commodity, and securities loans whose collateral or repayment prospects have weakened. It reviews government and external obligations, foreign exchange, declining gold reserves, note issuance, and price levels. Industry sections cover cement, copper, shipping, silk, cotton, and electric power; the closing excerpt anticipates substantial government borrowing. The surviving pages skip portions of the original report.

subfiles.title: Paris telegram 314 on French loan obstacles
subfiles.about: French Treasury officials deny negotiations and cite the unresolved Tokyo municipal bond dispute.
subfiles.summary: A Treasury official says no Japanese loan has been made or negotiated and that France would withhold approval until Tokyo satisfies a Dijon court judgment protecting French bondholders. The telegram discusses earlier refusal of a Japanese bond tranche and possible Mitsui purposes in Paris.

subfiles.title: New York Herald Tribune clipping
subfiles.about: A mixed clipping includes Manchurian railway claims and a report of the Nagasaki consulate fire.
subfiles.summary: Reports Tanaka Kōzō’s confession and snippets concerning China, Russia, and Manchuria.

subfiles.title: Duplicate last page of Paris telegram 314
subfiles.about: The page repeats the telegram’s speculation about Mitsui and the Tokyo bond judgment.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of page 53.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to despatch 800
subfiles.about: Locates a report on Takahashi’s call for cuts despite requests for additional budget items.
subfiles.summary: Cross-refers to a government finance report.

subfiles.title: Government finances extract
subfiles.about: Takahashi urges restraint while departments seek added funds and large loans loom.
subfiles.summary: Notes requests for agricultural and diplomatic funds and forthcoming budget and Bank of Japan bills.

subfiles.title: Lancaster message on a possible French advance
subfiles.from: Margaret Colgan, transmitting William W. Lancaster
subfiles.about: Lancaster reports hearsay that France advanced funds to Japan and was repaid in gold.
subfiles.summary: Amount and date are unknown.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Margaret Colgan
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges Lancaster’s report of a French advance.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Lancaster for bringing the information to the Department.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to telegram 366
subfiles.about: Locates a telegram on a proposed French loan to Manchukuo for the Chinese Eastern Railway.
subfiles.summary: Notes France’s refusal to sanction loans to either belligerent.

subfiles.title: Continuation of Paris telegram 366
subfiles.about: French officials reject meaningful financial support for Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: They doubt the Franco-Asiatic Bank can fund a substantial loan and say a public issue would lack official approval.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram 157 on approved budgets
subfiles.about: The Diet approves working and supplementary budgets with new Manchurian appropriations.
subfiles.summary: Lists additional army, navy, finance, and foreign affairs funds for June 1932 through January 1933.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to despatch 634
subfiles.about: Locates a despatch on proposed controls over capital leaving Japan.
subfiles.summary: Notes a bill to be introduced in the Diet.

subfiles.title: Unidentified securities fragment
subfiles.about: A surviving line refers to government treatment of a class of securities.
subfiles.summary: The fragment lacks enough text to identify its source.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to telegram 716
subfiles.about: Locates a report on seizure of customs funds by Manchukuo authorities.
subfiles.summary: Notes demands on the Bank of China and Bank of Chosen.

subfiles.title: Budget digest fragment
subfiles.about: A digest notes loan financing, tariff increases, and depression spending.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes high likely public borrowing costs and 70 million yen for economic relief.

subfiles.title: Despatch 20 on the approved supplementary budget
subfiles.about: The final supplementary budget funds Manchurian operations, economic relief, and other expenditures through borrowing.
subfiles.summary: The Diet’s June 14 budget contains roughly 301 million yen in supplementary spending and 364.54 million yen in loans. The despatch details military costs, tariff increases, Bank of Japan profits, depression relief, and measures against political radicalism. It estimates total remaining fiscal-year borrowing at about 529.5 million yen and enumerates earlier Manchuria and Shanghai campaign funds.

subfiles.title: Peiping telegram 828 reporting new bonds
subfiles.about: A Reuters report says Japan will issue bonds for military expenses in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Reports a 40 million yen issue at 90, paying five percent.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to despatch 38
subfiles.about: Locates a despatch on the 62nd Imperial Diet’s passage of the supplementary budget.
subfiles.summary: Cross-refers to despatch 38.

subfiles.title: Government finance section on the supplementary budget
subfiles.about: An excerpt summarizes military appropriations and bond issues approved in June.
subfiles.summary: Records 182.956 million yen for Manchuria and Shanghai, 364.54 million yen in bonds, and depression relief.

subfiles.title: Despatch 30 on proceedings of the 62nd Diet
subfiles.about: The extraordinary Diet session passes budget, bond, banking, tariff, capital-control, and silk measures.
subfiles.summary: The despatch lists the session’s budget estimates and enacted bills, including expanded Bank of Japan note issuance, foreign exchange controls, tariff changes, and raw-silk financing. It records Baron Sakatani’s warning about debt and Mr. Sugiyama’s criticism of the army’s political role. The embassy concludes that finance, farm distress, and recognition of Manchuria dominated debate.
